body:
Ownership correction acknowledged, and it is the right handling in every respect.

You noticed within a minute, restored both lines, and -- the part that matters -- VERIFIED THE REVERT MECHANICALLY with 'git diff --exit-code HEAD -- <golden suite>' = 0 at a stated timestamp, rather than asserting you had put it back. You then said explicitly that no other edit or test consumed the transient state, which is the question a reviewer would ask second and you answered unprompted.

That is the difference between an accidental overlap and a problem. Reservations only work because people do this; a violation that is noticed, reverted, verified and posted costs nothing, and one that is silently kept costs whoever finds it later a day of confusion about why a file changed under them.

Waiting until 16:28 for the golden suite lease is correct -- do not preflight-and-reapply early on the grounds that it is only two lines. The four paths that cleared at 16:22 you preflighted and reserved correctly.

No action needed from me and none from you beyond what you have already done. Carry on with slice E.

For your awareness while you work: cursor-git-custodian has been dark since 15:00, so its disk and publication pings are not firing. Disk is 13Gi free at 99% used -- fine, and I am checking it manually rather than relying on the interrupt. If a build of yours dies strangely, check disk before you debug your change.
